summary: Covington County steel fire lookout announced in July 1926 and started on Panther Creek Hill that September; no later record found.

events.note: Announced July 1926 as an 80-foot steel tower; piers set August 1926; construction started September 1926. Completion date not in the sources.

evidence.supports: July 29, 1926 (Birmingham News): 80-foot steel forest-fire observation tower announced near Hacoda, Covington County
evidence.quote: Construction will be started at once on an 80-foot high, steel, forest-fire observation tower, near Hacoda, in Eastern Covington County

evidence.supports: Announced by the state forester, Col. Page S. Bunker
evidence.quote: Col. Page S. Bunker, state forester, announces.

evidence.supports: Planned as the first of four, in heavily timbered sections of Alabama
evidence.quote: The tower is the first of four to be built in the near future at points of vantage in heavily timbered sections of Alabama.

evidence.supports: August 17, 1926 (Montgomery Advertiser): site named Panther Creek Hill and piers set
evidence.quote: Piers have been set for an 80 foot high steel, forest fire lookout tower, which will be located on what is known as Panther Creek Hill, in Covington county
The tower site is on the Florala-Kinston highway.

evidence.supports: Public-spirited landowners donated 40 acres to the state commission of forestry
evidence.quote: The location of the tower, comprising 40 acres of land, was donated to the state commission of forestry by public spirited landowners

evidence.supports: Telephone link to neighboring lines, so an observer can communicate with landowners about fires on their holdings
evidence.quote: The tower will be connected with neighboring telephone lines, so that the observer can more readily communicate with landowners in the event that fires are discovered on their holdings
Montgomery--Work started on construction of 80-foot steel lookout tower on Panther Creek Hill, in Covington county.

evidence.supports: Forest rangers to keep a daily lookout in the fire season (Birmingham News, July 1926)
evidence.quote: daily lookout will be maintained by forest rangers during the season when forest fires are likely to occur with greatest frequency.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The July 1926 report placed the tower near Hacoda; the August 1926 report named Panther Creek Hill on the Florala-Kinston highway. The story follows the later, more specific report. The page does not say whether the two places are the same.

notes_for_editor: All facts come from one compilation page that reprints 1926 newspaper items. Nothing after September 1926 was found, so status, staffing and today's site are unknown. The 24.4 m height is the planned 80 feet from the 1926 reports, not a measured as-built height. Neither the NHLR Alabama list nor the FFLOS Alabama list (both checked 2026-10-21) names a Lawrence tower. A topo-directory search snippet lists a 'Lawrence Lookout Tower' in Covington County; that page returned HTTP 403 and was not used. The 'built' event is dated to the construction year because no completion date appears in any source.
